Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear acceptance gates for the 3-week POC we discussed. I pulled these from the call and from Marissa's notes — please flag anything missing.

High-level success criteria (what Oceantech needs to validate):
- Functional: LLM generation meets your reranking throughput for 2k QPS equivalent (average latency < 300ms for 128-token outputs) across sample dataset A.
- Quality: Precision@5 on your 10k evaluation prompts >= 0.78 (baseline provided in shared sheet).
- Integration: Streaming SDK (JS + Python) integrated into a staging route with tool-calling support to your internal retrieval service.
- Ops: End-to-end telemetry (latency, tokens, error rates) visible in Redwood Console; basic alert if error-rate > 1%/5m.

Proposed timeline (three-week sprint):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW and access (we attached v1) — DocuSign link below.
- Week 1: SDK + streaming route integration (Marissa leads); mocking retrieval endpoints for tool calling.
- Week 2: Run evaluation suite, tune batching/quantization and measure latency/cost.
- Week 3: Acceptance run, final report and recommended config for production.

Owners and next actions:
- Vanessa (account): get SOW signed and coordinate procurement timeline.
- Marissa (solutions): lead integration, provide SDK routing example, streaming code snippet, and one-hour live pairing session.
- Neha (CS): set up Redwood Console dashboard + alerts, export baseline metrics.

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful and captures the discussion. A few clarifications/questions from our side:

1) Metrics: For Precision@5 we typically run against a gold set that includes context of up to 512 tokens — does your latency target assume the 128-token output with that context length? If not, please list the latency expectation per context length.

2) Streaming & tool calling: Priya wants to confirm that Redwood's streaming path allows mid-generation tool calls (we call out to a retrieval microservice during generation). If not, can Marissa outline a recommended approach for tool-calling patterns (pre-retrieval vs. mid-generation)?

3) Auth/access: We have a strict onboarding window for service accounts — can you confirm the minimum firewall/VPC info you need so our infra team can open access?

4) Finally, can you share a short example of the SDK route name and expected payload for streaming so our devs can begin building mocks?

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with Marissa. Fri 10:00–11:00 PT works for our engineers if that's open.

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Short answers up front, followed by an integration plan you can paste into your sprint board.

1) Latency vs. context length: Our stated 300ms budget was based on 128-token outputs with ~256 token context. For 512 token context expect +60–90ms overhead; we'll provide measured profiles after the first integration run.

2) Tool calling patterns: Redwood supports two patterns: pre-retrieval (call retrieval, then generate) and orchestrated mid-generation using the function/tool-calling hook. Mid-generation tool calls are permitted but require a lightweight external callback (we return a streaming hold event, call your retrieval endpoint, then resume generation). For the POC we recommend pre-retrieval for determinism, unless you specifically need incremental retrieval. I'll include both snippets.

3) Firewall/VPC: Minimums — allow outbound to api.redwood.example.com on 443 and open inbound from our health-check IP range for the staging route peering (listed below). If you need VPC peering we can open an RFC and involve infra.

4) SDK / streaming example route (minimal):
- Route name: /v1/redwood/streams/ot-poc
- Auth: Bearer token (service account)
- Payload (HTTP/2 streaming): initial JSON meta block with prompt/context, then stream of "token" events. See attached redwood_sdk_integration_notes.pdf for full example (JS & Python).

Integration plan (copy to your sprint):
- Day 0: Get SOW signed + provide service account.
- Day 1: Redwood creates staging model route /v1/redwood/streams/ot-poc and shares CA + token.
- Day 2–3: Your engineers wire SDK streaming client to mock retrieval endpoint; Marissa pairs for 1 hr.
- Day 4–6: Run 2x baseline evaluation runs; adjust batching and KV cache config.
- Day 7–10: Acceptance run and telemetry review with Neha.

Pairing times: I can do Fri 10:00 PT (Alex's suggested window) or Mon 09:00 PT — tell me which and I'll send an invite with a short agenda (code pairing + smoke test).

Notes: attaching the SDK snippet and a minimal curl example for streaming and auth.

—Marissa
